name: Caffeine
description: A rebuilt web indexing system. Google said it returned 50 percent fresher results and was the largest index it had ever run.
hint: Named after what keeps engineers awake.

name: Panda
description: An algorithm change touching 11.8 percent of US queries, built to push down thin, copied and low-quality pages from content farms.
hint: The first of the black and white animals.

name: Page Layout Algorithm
description: Demoted pages where visitors had to scroll past a wall of ads before reaching any real content.
hint: It judged what you see before you scroll.

name: Penguin
description: A webspam update aimed at keyword stuffing and link schemes, hitting sites that bought or built manipulative links.
hint: A black and white bird, a year after a black and white bear.

name: Pirate
description: Made the number of valid copyright removal notices against a site a ranking signal, pushing down repeat infringers.
hint: It reads DMCA notices like a treasure map.

name: Payday Loan
description: Targeted especially spammy query spaces like short-term loans and casinos, where spam ran deepest.
hint: Named for one of the spammiest queries on the web.

name: Hummingbird
description: A whole new core search algorithm, built to understand the meaning of full conversational queries instead of matching single keywords.
hint: Small, fast, precise, and a bird.

name: Pigeon
description: Tied local search rankings more closely to traditional web ranking signals, reshuffling local packs and Maps results.
hint: A bird that always finds its way home.

name: Doorway Pages Update
description: A ranking adjustment against pages built only to funnel search traffic, like near-identical city pages that all lead to one site.
hint: You walk through it to get somewhere else.

name: Mobilegeddon
description: Made mobile-friendliness a ranking signal for searches on phones. Desktop results were untouched.
hint: The industry named it like a disaster movie.

name: RankBrain
description: Google's first machine learning system in ranking, used to interpret queries it had never seen before.
hint: A brain, for ranking.

name: Penguin 4.0
description: The link spam filter joined the core algorithm and went real-time, devaluing bad links instead of demoting whole sites.
hint: The 2012 bird, now running all the time.

name: Intrusive Interstitials
description: Pages that covered their content with pop-ups on the jump from mobile results could start ranking lower.
hint: About the thing standing between you and the page.

name: Fred
description: A quality update the community named itself. It hit ad-heavy, low-value sites written for revenue instead of readers.
hint: Named as a joke, with a regular guy's first name.

name: Speed Update
description: Page speed became a ranking factor for mobile searches, though Google said only the slowest pages would be affected.
hint: Only the slowest pages felt it.

name: Medic
description: A broad core update that hit health, wellness and other your-money-or-your-life sites hardest.
hint: Named for the kind of sites it hit.

name: Site Diversity Update
description: Limited most queries to no more than two results from the same domain.
hint: About variety on page one.

name: Link Attributes Update
description: Added the sponsored and ugc link attributes and turned nofollow from a directive into a hint.
hint: rel= got two new siblings.

name: BERT
description: A transformer language model applied to ranking. Google said it helped understand about one in 10 English searches in the US.
hint: Shares a name with a Sesame Street character.

name: Passage Ranking
description: Let Google rank a single passage buried deep in a long page, not just the page as a whole.
hint: The needle, not the haystack.

name: April 2021 Product Reviews Update
description: The first update of its kind: it rewarded in-depth reviews with original research over thin summaries of a product's specs.
hint: Affiliate sites felt this one first.

name: MUM
description: A multimodal AI model Google called 1,000 times more powerful than BERT, able to read text and images together.
hint: Three letters, and it sounds like a parent.

name: Page Experience Update
description: Made Core Web Vitals, along with mobile-friendliness, HTTPS and no intrusive interstitials, a ranking signal on mobile.
hint: The umbrella over LCP, FID and CLS.

name: July 2021 Link Spam Update
description: Set out to nullify link spam across languages, with a reminder to tag sponsored and affiliate links properly.
hint: Came with a lecture on rel=sponsored.

name: November 2021 Core Update
description: A core update that landed nine days before Black Friday, with a product reviews update following two weeks later.
hint: Bad timing for retailers.

name: December 2021 Product Reviews Update
description: The second update of its kind, rolling out for 20 days through the holiday shopping season.
hint: Shopping season, second edition.

name: Page Experience Update for Desktop
description: Took the Core Web Vitals ranking signal from phones to the bigger screen.
hint: Same signal, bigger screen.

name: May 2022 Core Update
description: The first core update in six months, with YMYL and health sites moving most.
hint: Arrived in late spring after a long quiet stretch.

name: August 2022 Helpful Content Update
description: Introduced a site-wide signal that demoted content made mainly for search engines instead of people.
hint: People-first, the very first time.

name: September 2022 Core Update
description: A core update that overlapped with a product reviews update starting eight days later, making the two hard to separate.
hint: Back to school, with company.

name: October 2022 Spam Update
description: A spam update that finished in two days, the fastest one Google had shipped up to then.
hint: Over before Halloween.

name: December 2022 Helpful Content Update
description: Took the site-wide unhelpful content signal global, over a 38-day rollout through the holidays.
hint: The second time, and worldwide.

name: December 2022 Link Spam Update
description: Used SpamBrain to neutralize unnatural links at scale, aimed at buying links and at sites built to pass them.
hint: A 29-day holiday gift for PBN owners.

name: February 2023 Product Reviews Update
description: Expanded product review ranking beyond English to 10 more languages, the last update to carry the word product.
hint: The shortest month got the last one with this name.

name: March 2023 Core Update
description: The first core update of 2023, landing about three weeks after a reviews update.
hint: Spring's first core rollout of that year.

name: April 2023 Reviews Update
description: Dropped the word product: reviews of services, businesses, destinations and media were now in scope.
hint: It lost a word from its name.

name: August 2023 Core Update
description: A core update that finished one week before a far more damaging helpful content update began.
hint: The calm before the September storm.

name: September 2023 Helpful Content Update
description: The last standalone update of its kind. Many affiliate and content sites lost half their traffic or more.
hint: The one niche site owners still talk about.

name: October 2023 Spam Update
description: A spam update aimed at cloaking, hacked, auto-generated and scraped spam in many non-English languages.
hint: Spam detection learned more languages.

name: October 2023 Core Update
description: A core update that ran alongside a separate ranking issue on the dashboard, one that hurt Discover traffic.
hint: Started one day after a spam update.

name: November 2023 Core Update
description: The second core update in two months, starting just two weeks after the previous one finished.
hint: Back to back, autumn edition.

name: November 2023 Reviews Update
description: The last announced update of its kind. Google said the system would improve continuously from then on, without notice.
hint: The last one we got told about.

name: March 2024 Core Update
description: The longest core rollout on record at 45 days, and the one that folded the helpful content system into core ranking.
hint: It absorbed a whole system.

name: March 2024 Spam Update
description: Shipped with three new spam policies: scaled content abuse, expired domain abuse and site reputation abuse.
hint: Three new policies, same day as a giant core update.

name: Site Reputation Abuse Enforcement
description: Enforcement began against third-party pages riding a host site's ranking signals, like coupon sections on news sites.
hint: Parasite SEO, finally named.

name: AI Overviews Launch
description: AI-generated summaries at the top of results began rolling out to everyone in the US, announced at Google I/O.
hint: Gemini moved above the ten blue links.

name: June 2024 Spam Update
description: A week-long spam update in early summer, six weeks after a new policy on third-party content started being enforced.
hint: Summer's spam cleanup.

name: Explicit Fake Content Update
description: Made removal easier for non-consensual intimate imagery generated with AI, and demoted sites that host a lot of it.
hint: Deepfakes.

name: August 2024 Core Update
description: A core update shaped by creator feedback, where some sites hit by the 2023 helpful content update recovered.
hint: Some September 2023 casualties got a second look.

name: AI Overviews Expands to Six Countries
description: AI summaries in search left the US for six new countries, months after Google pulled back some of their answers.
hint: The first trip abroad.

name: AI Overviews Expands to 100+ Countries
description: AI summaries reached more than 100 countries, putting them in front of over a billion users a month.
hint: The largest expansion, and the billion-user mark.

name: November 2024 Core Update
description: A core update lasting more than three weeks, followed by another core update one week after it finished.
hint: The first of two in about a month.

name: Site Reputation Abuse Policy Update
description: Clarified that first-party involvement or oversight does not protect third-party content published to exploit a host site.
hint: No more white-label loophole.

name: December 2024 Core Update
description: An unusually fast core update, done in six days, just one week after the previous core update finished.
hint: Six days, right before the holidays.

name: December 2024 Spam Update
description: A week-long spam update that ran straight through Christmas.
hint: Coal in the stocking.

name: March 2025 Core Update
description: The first core update of its year, finished in two weeks after a three-month quiet stretch.
hint: Spring, mid-decade.

name: AI Mode
description: A full conversational search mode powered by Gemini started rolling out to everyone in the US, announced at Google I/O.
hint: Not an overview. A whole mode.

name: June 2025 Core Update
description: A core update that started on the last day of its month, with some sites hit by earlier helpful content and reviews updates partly recovering.
hint: Started on the last day of the month.

name: August 2025 Spam Update
description: A spam update that took nearly four weeks, far longer than the few days spam updates usually need.
hint: Late summer, and it would not end.

name: December 2025 Core Update
description: The third core update of its year, running 18 days through the holidays.
hint: A holiday core update, mid-decade.

name: February 2026 Discover Update
description: The first core update scoped only to the feed, not Search results, starting with English-language users in the US.
hint: It never showed up in Search performance reports.

name: March 2026 Spam Update
description: The fastest spam update on record, finished in about 19 and a half hours.
hint: Done in under a day.

name: March 2026 Core Update
description: The first Search core update of its year, starting three days after a spam update that finished in under a day.
hint: Spring, right after the shortest spam update.

name: May 2026 Core Update
description: The second Search core update of its year, finished in about 12 days in early June.
hint: Late spring, this year.

name: June 2026 Spam Update
description: A two-day spam update, the second of its year, widely read as aimed at low-effort templated content.
hint: Midsummer, this year.

name: August 2026 Spam Update
description: The third spam update of its year, finished in under three days with no new spam policies.
hint: Late summer, this year.

name: September 2026 Spam Update
description: The fourth spam update of its year, which Google said could take up to two weeks to finish.
hint: The newest one on the list.
